svg.aria-label: Shrinking a video on import. In Enzo’s gallery, three videos are added, and the screen says “Encrypting the video, 1 of 3”, then “Shrinking the video” with its percentage. The first, shot on the phone at 1080 x 1920 and 16 Mb/s, weighs 20 MB: Media3 re-encodes it on the phone encoder, in H.264, 720 points on the short side, 2.5 Mb/s, sound as is. It comes out at 3 MB, under the 90% line: the shrunk one enters the vault and the original is deleted. The second, already compressed at 2.7 Mb/s, weighs 8 MB; re-encoded, it still takes 7.6, above the 7.2 line: the shrunk one is deleted and the original goes in. The third, 720 x 1280 at 3 Mb/s, is already under both limits, 720 points and 4 Mb/s: it goes in without touching the encoder. If the encoder fails, its output is deleted and the original goes in. In all, 33 MB picked, 16 MB in the vault, every video encrypted in chunks.

svg.text: A video shot for a big screen, brought down to what you watch on a phone. Only when it is worth it.

g.text: 3 videos: 33 MB picked, 16 MB in the vault.
720 on the short side, 3 Mb/s: under both limits.
33 MB picked, 16 MB in the vault.
Every video goes in chunk-encrypted, shrunk or not.

svg.text: 720 or less on the short side
and 4 Mb/s at most: left alone.
H.264, 720 on the short side, 2.5 Mb/s,
sound as is, on the phone encoder.

g.text: The original is deleted from the cache.
The shrunk one, 7.6 MB, is deleted.
One by one, the lighter of the two,

svg.text: Its output is deleted, the original goes
into the vault and the import carries on.
A phone films in 4K at 50 Mb/s. Kept as is,
the vault and the backups swell.
The length and the thumbnail frame are
read from the original, still in the clear.
During the import nobody touches the
screen: the delay cuts nothing short.
